Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 57, verses 1–6:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Sabbaha lillahi ma fi as-samawati wal-ard﴾: that is, Allah the Exalted is glorified and declared free of imperfection by everything in the heavens and the earth, through the tongue of disposition and the tongue of speech.

﴿Wa huwa al-'Aziz al-Hakim﴾: that is, the Mighty in His dominion, the Wise in His creation and His governance.

﴿Lahu mulku as-samawati wal-ard﴾: that is, He owns everything in the heavens and the earth and disposes of it as He wills.

﴿Yuhyi wa yumit﴾: He gives life after non-existence, and He causes death after existence and life.

﴿Wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir﴾: and He is capable of doing whatever He wills; nothing can overcome Him.

﴿Huwa al-Awwalu wal-Akhir﴾: that is, nothing is before Him, and He is the Last after whom nothing remains.

﴿Wal-Zahiru wal-Batin﴾: that is, the Outward, above whom nothing is, and the Inward, beneath whom nothing is.

﴿Wa huwa bikulli shay'in 'alim﴾: that is, nothing is hidden from His knowledge, not even the weight of an atom in the heavens and the earth.

﴿Fi sittati ayyam﴾: that is, in days of this worldly life, measured by them, the first of which is Sunday and the last of which is Friday.

﴿Thumma istawa 'ala al-'Arsh﴾: that is, He rose over it and ascended.

﴿Ya'lamu ma yalju fi al-ard﴾: that is, what enters the earth of all that enters it, such as rain and the dead.

﴿Wa ma yakhruju minha﴾: that is, of plants and minerals.

﴿Wa ma yanzilu min as-sama'﴾: that is, of mercy and punishment.

﴿Wa ma ya'ruju fiha﴾: that is, what ascends into it of righteous and evil deeds.

﴿Wa huwa ma'akum ayna kuntum﴾: that is, by His knowledge of you and His power over you, wherever you are.

﴿Wallahu bima ta'malsuna basir﴾: that is, nothing of the outward and inward deeds of His servants is hidden from Him.

﴿Wa ila Allahi turja'u al-umur﴾: that is, the return of all things is to Allah, their Creator and Governor, who judges in them as He wills.

﴿Yuliju al-layla fi an-nahar﴾: that is, He makes part of the night enter the day, and this happens in summer.

﴿Wa yuliju an-nahara fi al-layl﴾: and He makes part of the day enter the night, and this happens in winter, just as each of them may enter wholly into the other, so that only night or only day remains, since one of them has entered the other.

﴿Wa huwa 'alimun bidhati as-sudur﴾: that is, what is in the breasts of beliefs, secrets and intentions.

Meaning of the verses:

In these five verses, the Exalted informs of His existence and greatness: His power, knowledge, wisdom, mercy, governance, dominion, and that all matters return to Him. All of these are manifestations of lordship that necessitate divinity. First, all that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, that is, declares Him free from every deficiency, such as a spouse, a child, a partner, an appointed minister, weakness and ignorance. Second, He is the Mighty, possessing a might that cannot be challenged, the Great in retribution, the Wise in governing His dominion, so nothing in His creation is in vain, idle or false. Third, to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, a true dominion; He disposes of it as He wills, giving to whom He wills and withholding from whom He wills. Fourth, He gives life from non-existence and causes the living, existing being to die. Fifth, He is capable of all things; nothing overcomes Him, and He is not incapable of anything. Whenever He wills a thing and says to it "Be," it is, without fail.

Sixth: He is the First, before whom nothing is, and the Last, after whom nothing is, for to Him belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth. Seventh: His knowledge encompasses everything. Eighth: He created the heavens and the earth in six days of this worldly life, beginning on Sunday and ending on Friday, and no fatigue, weariness or exhaustion touched Him. Then He rose over the Throne, governing the dominion of His creation with wisdom and manifestations of justice and mercy. Ninth: despite His loftiness above His creation, all creation is before Him. He knows what enters the earth, that is, rain and the dead, and what descends from the sky, such as rain, mercy, punishment, angels and others, and what ascends into it, such as angels, righteous deeds and supplication, especially the supplication of the oppressed, for it is never veiled from Allah. Tenth: the companionship of Allah, both special and general. The special companionship is His support of His allies; the general is His knowledge of all His servants and all His creation, His power over them and His knowledge of them. Eleventh: His sight encompasses all the deeds of His servants, and nothing of them is hidden from Him, so that He may call them to account and recompense them for them. Twelfth: to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that is, all creation in the heavens and the earth is the possession of Allah alone, with no partner in it or in anything else. Thirteenth: all matters return to Him, so none judges in them but Him, and none decides them but Him, and what is apparent of them is like what is hidden. Fourteenth: His causing the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night is for the benefit and advantage of His servants, for without this wise governance the affairs of life would not be sound and this existence would not be upright.

Finally, His knowledge encompasses everything and penetrates every hidden thing, even the innermost thoughts of the breast: whisperings, suggestions, concerns, resolutions, intentions and wills. Glory be to Him, a God besides whom there is no god, and no lord other than Him. By these manifestations of perfection He deserves worship, so worship is not valid for other than Him, and obedience is not fitting for anyone but Him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The excellence of glorification, and its most excellent form: "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi, Subhan Allah al-'Azim."

2- The manifestations of power, knowledge and wisdom in these five verses are the grounds of Allah's lordship and divinity, and they necessitate the Final Resurrection and recompense therein.

3- Allah's creation of the heavens and the earth in six days, though He is capable of creating them by the word of command, teaches His servants patience in affairs and avoidance of haste, so that they come out perfected, sound and beneficial.

4- The invalidity of calling upon other than Allah and hoping in other than Him, since to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and nothing of that belongs to anyone else.

5- The obligation of watching over Allah, feeling shame before Him and fearing Him, because of His knowledge of our outward and inward states and His power to recompense us, in this world and the next.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 57, verse 7–11:

Explanation of the words:

"Believe in Allah and His Messenger": That is, affirm belief in Allah and His Messenger, O you who have not yet believed, and remain steadfast in your faith, O you who believed before.

"So those of you who believe and spend": That is, those who affirm belief in Allah and His Messenger and give charity from their wealth, of which they are successors.

"For them is a great reward": That is, a mighty reward with Allah, and it is Paradise.

"And what is [the matter] with you that you do not believe in Allah?": That is, what prevents you from believing?

"While the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord": That is, while the Messenger himself invites you to believe in your Lord.

"And He has already taken your covenant": That is, to believe in Him, when you were in the realm of the particles (alam al-dharr), when He made you bear witness and you bore witness.

"If you are believers": That is, if you are desiring belief, then do not hesitate; believe and submit, that you may be saved and made happy.

"It is He who sends down to His servant": That is, He is Allah, your Lord, to whom His Messenger invites you that you believe; He sends down to His servant Muhammad ﷺ.

"Clear signs": These are the clear verses of the Noble Qur'an, plain in meaning and evident in indication.

"To bring you out from darkness into light": That is, to bring you out from the darknesses of disbelief and ignorance into the light of faith and knowledge.

"And indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to you": His sending of His Messenger to you and His sending down of His Book, to bring you out from darkness into light, is evidence of this.

"And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the way of Allah?": That is, what reason do you have for not spending in the way of Allah?

"And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth": That is, and from that wealth which is in your hands, it returns to Allah, so spend it in His way and He will reward you for it; otherwise it will return to Him without any reward for you.

"Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest": That is, they are not equal to those who spent and fought after the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, when Islam became mighty and the wealth of the Muslims increased.

"And to each Allah has promised the best": That is, Paradise, and Paradise has degrees.

"Who is it that will loan Allah a goodly loan?": That is, by spending his wealth in the way of Allah, which is jihad.

"A goodly loan": That is, a loan intended for nothing but the Face of Allah, the Exalted.

"And He will multiply it for him": That is, one dirham for seven hundred dirhams.

"And he will have a noble reward": That is, on the Day of Resurrection, which is Paradise, the abode of lasting bliss.

Meaning of the verses:

After mentioning the proofs and evidences of the existence of Allah, His power, knowledge and wisdom, the obligation of worshipping Him and His unity in worship, and the establishment of resurrection and recompense on the Day of meeting Him, out of His mercy and compassion for His servants, He commanded them all, believers and disbelievers, to have faith in Him and in His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ. The believers are commanded to increase their faith and remain steadfast in it, and the disbelievers are commanded to believe and to hasten to it. Since this verse was revealed in Medina after the Hijrah and after the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, these divine commands and directives include sincere believers and hypocrites who are false in their faith, and they include those in Mecca and elsewhere who desire faith but hesitate. So the address is directed to all of them for their guidance and their entry into the mercy of Allah, Islam, swiftly and without delay. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, affirm the oneness of Allah and the message of the Messenger of Allah, "and spend of that in which He has made you successors" of the wealth. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So those of you who believe and spend, for them is a great reward﴾, that is, a mighty reward with Allah, which is Paradise and its good pleasure. This information serves to stir up lukewarm resolves and hesitant determinations. Your innate faith is clear within your souls, for whenever anyone asks you: Who created you? Who created the world around you, heavens and earth? You say: Allah. You are within His sanctuary and the protected zone of His House, and the Noble Messenger is before you, inviting you morning and evening to believe in your Lord. Allah has taken your covenant upon you to believe in Him, on the day He brought you forth in the form of particles from the loins of Adam, your father, and made you bear witness against yourselves, and you bore witness. So what is this hesitation? If you truly want to believe, then believe before it is too late.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿It is He who sends down upon His servant clear signs﴾, that is, you are being called to believe in Allah, who sends down upon His servant and Messenger Muhammad ﷺ signs clear in meaning and evident in proof, all of that "to bring you out from darkness into light", from the darknesses of disbelief and ignorance into the light of faith and knowledge. So why do you not believe? What then is this hesitation and reluctance, O servants of Allah, in believing in Allah and in the Messenger of Allah? "Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to you", so recognize this and believe in Him. His sending down the Book, His sending the Messenger, and His clarifying the proofs and establishing the arguments and evidences indicate this.

As for His saying: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the way of Allah﴾, which is the way of your happiness and perfection after your salvation from punishment in both lives, with the knowledge that to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, since what is in your hands belongs to Allah; He is its giver to you and its reclaimer from you, so why do you not spend from it?

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest﴾, that is, the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, according to the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest﴾ [al-Fath: 1], and the intended meaning is the Treaty of Hudaybiyah. That is, they are not equal in reward and recompense with those who fought and spent after the conquest. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought. But to each Allah has promised the best﴾ of the two groups, ﴿the best﴾, that is, Paradise, ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾, nothing of your spending, fighting, or abstention is hidden from Him, just as your intentions and what you conceal within yourselves are not hidden from Him, so beware of Him and be watchful of Him, for that is better for you.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Who is it that will loan Allah a goodly loan﴾, that is, sincerely for Allah, with his soul content in giving it, ﴿so He will multiply it for him﴾ by his Lord, one dirham into seven hundred dirhams, ﴿and he will have a noble reward﴾, which is Paradise, the abode of peace.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The obligation of faith in Allah and His Messenger, and strengthening it.

2- The obligation of spending in the way of Allah, from zakat, expenditure for jihad, and charity to the poor and needy.

3- Clarification of Allah's kindness, compassion and mercy toward His servants, which necessitates loving Him, obeying Him and thanking Him.

4- Spending during famines, hardships and war is better than spending in ease and well-being.

5- Encouragement to spend in the way of Allah by multiplication of reward, to the point that a dinar becomes a thousand dinars with Allah, the Exalted, and what is with Allah is better and more lasting, and the Hereafter is better than the first.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 57, Verses 12–15**

**Explanation of the words:**

﴿يَسْعَى نُورُهُم بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾: i.e., their light, which they gained through faith and righteous deeds, goes before them over great distances, lighting for them the path (ṣirāṭ) they cross to Paradise.

﴿بُشْرَاكُمُ الْيَوْمَ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ﴾: i.e., the angels who have been appointed to receive them say to them: "Glad tidings to you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow."

﴿ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾: i.e., deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise is the great triumph, greater than which there is none.

﴿الْمُنَافِقُونَ وَالْمُنَافِقَاتُ﴾: i.e., those who concealed disbelief in their souls while showing faith and Islam with their tongues.

﴿تَقْتَبِسْ مِن نُّورِكُمْ﴾: i.e., "Look at us with your faces, so that we may take from your light that which will illuminate the way for us."

﴿قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وَرَاءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُوراً﴾: i.e., it will be said to them mockingly: "Go back behind you to the world, where light is sought through faith and righteous deeds, after abandoning shirk and sins." So they turn back behind them, but find nothing.

﴿فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهُم بِسُورٍ لَّهُ بَابٌ بَاطِنُهُ الرَّحْمَةُ﴾: i.e., a high wall is set up between them and the believers, having a gate whose inner side, facing the believers, is mercy.

﴿وَظَاهِرُهُ مِن قِبَلِهِ الْعَذَابُ﴾: i.e., its outer side, facing the hypocrites on the plain of Resurrection, is punishment.

﴿يُنَادُونَهُمْ أَلَمْ نَكُن مَّعَكُمْ﴾: i.e., the hypocrites call out to the believers, saying: "Were we not with you in the world in acts of obedience, praying as you pray, striving as you strive, and spending as you spend?"

﴿قَالُوا بَلَى﴾: i.e., "Yes, you were with us in acts of obedience."

﴿وَلَكِنَّكُمْ فَتَنتُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ﴾: i.e., by hypocrisy, which is inner disbelief and hatred of Islam and the Muslims.

﴿وَتَرَبَّصْتُمْ﴾: i.e., you waited for the turns of fortune against the Muslims, awaiting the moment when the believers would be defeated, so that you could declare your disbelief and return to your polytheism.

﴿وَغَرَّكُم بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ﴾: i.e., you were deceived concerning faith in Allah and His Messenger, for Satan made disbelief attractive to you and made faith hateful to you.

﴿فَالْيَوْمَ لَا يُؤْخَذُ مِنكُمْ فِدْيَةٌ﴾: i.e., no ransom, no wealth by which you might redeem yourselves, since on that day neither wealth nor children will benefit.

﴿وَلَا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾: i.e., nor will any ransom be accepted from those who disbelieved.

﴿مَأْوَاكُمُ النَّارُ هِيَ مَوْلَاكُمْ﴾: i.e., your abode and place of lodging is the Fire; it is more fitting for you, because of the corruption of your souls.

﴿وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾: i.e., evil is the destination to which you have come, which is the Fire.

**The meaning of the verses:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾. This time-phrase is connected to the phrase ﴿وَلَهُ أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ at the end of the preceding verse: they have a noble reward on the day when you see the believing men and women on the plain of Resurrection, their light, which they gained through their faith and righteous deeds in the abode of the world. That light walks before them, guiding them to the path of Paradise, and their books have been given to them in their right hands. The angels appointed to receive and welcome them say: ﴿بُشْرَاكُمُ الْيَوْمَ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ﴾, meaning that rivers of water, milk, wine and honey flow through the trees and palaces, and they abide therein forever, never dying and never leaving. Allah says: ﴿ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾, for it is deliverance from the Fire and entry into the gardens in the neighborhood of the Most Merciful.

As for His words ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُولُ الْمُنَافِقُونَ وَالْمُنَافِقَاتُ﴾, it is a substitute (badal) for "the day when you see the believing men and women." The hypocrites (munāfiqūn) are those who, in worldly life, concealed disbelief in their souls and displayed faith with their tongues and Islam with their limbs. Then a high wall is set up between them and the believers, ﴿لَّهُ بَابٌ بَاطِنُهُ﴾, which is on the side of the believers and in which is mercy, ﴿وَظَاهِرُهُ﴾, which is on the side of the hypocrites, ﴿مِن قِبَلِهِ الْعَذَابُ﴾. Then they begin calling out: "Were we not with you, O believers, in acts of obedience? We prayed with you, struggled with you, and spent as you spent." The believers reply: ﴿بَلَى﴾, i.e., "You were with us in the world in acts of obedience outwardly, but you ﴿فَتَنتُمْ أَنفُسَكُم﴾ by hypocrisy, and ﴿تَرَبَّصْتُم﴾ against us the turns of fortune, so that you might declare your disbelief and return to your polytheism. ﴿وَارْتَبتُمْ﴾, i.e., you doubted the truth of Islam and its doctrines, including the resurrection of the Hereafter. ﴿وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْأَمَانِيُّ﴾, the false wishes and hopes that Muhammad would not triumph and his religion would not prevail, until ﴿جَاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾, the command of Allah to grant victory to His Messenger and make His religion manifest. ﴿وَغَرَّكُم بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ﴾, i.e., by faith in Allah, after He hastened punishment against you, concealed you, did not expose you, and did not reveal to others the disbelief you were upon. ﴿الْغَرُورُ﴾ is Satan, for he is the one who made disbelief attractive to you and reminded you of Allah's pardon and His not seizing you immediately.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Affirmation of the Resurrection, mentioning its events and what takes place in it.

2. Affirmation that true triumph is not the gain of a sheep or a camel, nor a house or a garden in this world, but rather being drawn away from the Fire and admitted into the gardens on the Day of Resurrection; this is the great triumph.

3. Among the glad tidings of happiness for the people of faith before entering Paradise: the angels' welcome of them, their being given their books in their right hands, and the presence of a high light going before them and on their right, leading them over the ṣirāṭ to Paradise.

4. There is light on the Day of Resurrection in the faces of the believers, which they took from this world. The hadith says: «Give good tidings to those who walk in darkness to the mosques with complete light on the Day of Resurrection.»

5. Description of the attributes of the hypocrites in this world: concealing disbelief in their souls, lying in wait for the believers in order to pounce on them whenever they are weakened or defeated, and their wishes that Islam would not be supported. Their doubt clings to them so that they did not leave it until they died, doubting the truth of Islam and what it brought of promise and threat.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 57, verses 16–19:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Has the time not come for those who believe⦆: i.e., has the time not come for those who have been excessive in joking?

"that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah": i.e., that they should soften, become calm, submit and find rest in the remembrance of Allah and His promise and His threat.

"and what has come down of the truth": i.e., the Qur'an and what it contains of promise and threat.

"and not be like those who were given the Scripture before": i.e., and not be like the Jews and Christians in turning away and heedlessness.

"so the term grew long for them": i.e., the time between them and their prophets.

"so their hearts became hard": i.e., because there was no one to remind them and guide them, their hearts became hard and did not soften to the remembrance of Allah.

"and many of them are defiantly disobedient": i.e., as a result of the hardness of heart that follows from abandoning reminder and guidance, most of them became defiantly disobedient, departed from the religion of Allah and rejected His teachings.

"Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death": i.e., by the rain that descends upon it; likewise He gives life to hearts through remembrance and reminder, so they soften and humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah and His promise and threat.

"We have already made the signs clear to you, that you may use your reason": i.e., We have made clear to you the signs that indicate Our power, knowledge, kindness and mercy, in hope that you will understand and so protect yourselves from what destroys and ruins you.

"Indeed, the men who give charity and the women who give charity": i.e., those who give charity from the surplus of their wealth, and the women likewise.

"and lend to Allah a goodly loan": i.e., their charities were like a goodly loan, free of any reproach, with souls content in giving and hoping from their Lord for its reward.

"it will be multiplied for them": i.e., the goodly loan is multiplied tenfold, up to seven hundred, up to a thousand thousand.

"And those who believe in Allah and His messengers": i.e., who affirmed Allah as Lord and God, and His messengers as truthful guides and callers.

"those are the truthful (ṣiddīqūn)": i.e., those who are recorded before Allah as ṣiddīqūn, which is a high rank of honour.

"and the martyrs (shuhadā') with their Lord, they will have their reward and their light": i.e., and the martyrs of the battles in the way of Allah, with their Lord, i.e., in Paradise, they will have their great reward and their complete light on the Day of Resurrection.

"But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs": i.e., who disbelieved in Allah and His oneness and denied the Qur'an and what it contains of laws and rulings.

"those are the companions of the Hellfire": i.e., those far removed, who are the people of the Fire, from which they will never depart, forever.

Meaning of the verses:

The Almighty's saying ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe﴾: i.e., those who truly believe in Allah as Lord and God, and in Muhammad ﷺ, and in the promise and threat of Allah, has the time not come for them that their hearts should humble themselves, soften and be at rest in the remembrance of Allah, and likewise be humbled? ﴿and what has come down of the truth﴾ in the Noble Book, so that they recognise what is right, enjoin it, recognise what is wrong and forbid it. It is indeed a great divine admonition, and what makes it greater is that it was revealed concerning the companions of the Messenger of Allah, whose hearts were slow to respond. How then with those who came after them?

His saying: ﴿and not be like those who were given the Scripture before﴾: i.e., before the Muhammadan mission, namely the Jews and Christians. ﴿So the term grew long for them﴾: i.e., the long period between them and their prophets, so they were not reminded and not guided, and therefore their hearts became hard, and most of them became defiantly disobedient to the religion of Allah, departing from its laws, not recognising what is right nor denouncing what is wrong.

His Exalted saying ﴿Know﴾: i.e., you believers, afflicted by some heedlessness, whose joking and laughter have increased, ﴿that Allah gives life to the earth after its death﴾: He gives it life by rain, and it grows and flourishes. Likewise hearts die when reminder, direction and guidance are abandoned, and they live through reminder and guidance.

His Exalted saying: ﴿We have indeed made the signs clear to you﴾: i.e., We have explained them to you in this Noble Book, ﴿that you may use your reason﴾, i.e., that We may prepare you thereby to understand from Us what We address to you and advise you concerning, so remember this and do not forget it, and turn your hearts back and attend to them with the remembrance of Allah and the Last Abode.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the men who give charity﴾: i.e., those who give charity from the surplus of their wealth in the way of Allah, and the women who give charity likewise, and who lend to Allah a goodly loan by what they spend in jihad, their souls content in giving, with no reproach, no ostentation and no show. For these it will be multiplied: i.e., the reward of their charities and their loan to their Lord is multiplied tenfold, up to seven hundred times, up to a thousand thousand, and for them is a noble reward, which is Paradise. ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers﴾, who affirmed Allah as Lord and God, and the chosen messengers of Allah as guides to Allah and callers to Him: these are the ṣiddīqūn, and they attained the rank of ṣiddīqiyyah. The martyrs, those who were killed in the battles of jihad, are now with their Lord: they have their reward and their light, their souls are in the crops of green birds grazing in Paradise. These three categories are like the foremost (al-sābiqūn) and the companions of the right (aṣḥāb al-yamīn). ﴿And those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., in Allah and His messengers, ﴿and deny Our signs﴾, i.e., the signs of their Lord containing His laws and worship, so they did not worship Him by them: these are the lowest, ﴿the companions of the Hellfire﴾, who will abide in it and it will abide with them forever. We seek refuge in Allah from their state.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A warning against heedlessness and forgetting the remembrance of Allah, and of what He has of bliss and what He has of punishment and torment.

2- The obligation of reminding, admonishing, guiding and teaching believers, lest their hearts harden and they become defiantly disobedient as the People of the Book became disobedient, and disbelieve as they disbelieved.

3- Affirmation of the truth that the earth is revived by rain and hearts are revived by knowledge, admonitions and reminder of Allah.

4- Explanation of the categories of believers and their ranks: those who give charity and lend to Allah from their wealth in the way of Allah, the believers in Allah and His messengers in true faith, the ṣiddīqūn, and the martyrs of jihad in the way of Allah, may Allah make us among them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 57, verses 16–19:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Has the time not come for those who believe⦆: i.e., has the time not come for those who have been excessive in joking?

"that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah": i.e., that they should soften, become calm, submit and find rest in the remembrance of Allah and His promise and His threat.

"and what has come down of the truth": i.e., the Qur'an and what it contains of promise and threat.

"and not be like those who were given the Scripture before": i.e., and not be like the Jews and Christians in turning away and heedlessness.

"so the term grew long for them": i.e., the time between them and their prophets.

"so their hearts became hard": i.e., because there was no one to remind them and guide them, their hearts became hard and did not soften to the remembrance of Allah.

"and many of them are defiantly disobedient": i.e., as a result of the hardness of heart that follows from abandoning reminder and guidance, most of them became defiantly disobedient, departed from the religion of Allah and rejected His teachings.

"Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death": i.e., by the rain that descends upon it; likewise He gives life to hearts through remembrance and reminder, so they soften and humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah and His promise and threat.

"We have already made the signs clear to you, that you may use your reason": i.e., We have made clear to you the signs that indicate Our power, knowledge, kindness and mercy, in hope that you will understand and so protect yourselves from what destroys and ruins you.

"Indeed, the men who give charity and the women who give charity": i.e., those who give charity from the surplus of their wealth, and the women likewise.

"and lend to Allah a goodly loan": i.e., their charities were like a goodly loan, free of any reproach, with souls content in giving and hoping from their Lord for its reward.

"it will be multiplied for them": i.e., the goodly loan is multiplied tenfold, up to seven hundred, up to a thousand thousand.

"And those who believe in Allah and His messengers": i.e., who affirmed Allah as Lord and God, and His messengers as truthful guides and callers.

"those are the truthful (ṣiddīqūn)": i.e., those who are recorded before Allah as ṣiddīqūn, which is a high rank of honour.

"and the martyrs (shuhadā') with their Lord, they will have their reward and their light": i.e., and the martyrs of the battles in the way of Allah, with their Lord, i.e., in Paradise, they will have their great reward and their complete light on the Day of Resurrection.

"But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs": i.e., who disbelieved in Allah and His oneness and denied the Qur'an and what it contains of laws and rulings.

"those are the companions of the Hellfire": i.e., those far removed, who are the people of the Fire, from which they will never depart, forever.

**Explanation of the words (Sharh al-Kalimat):**

*Innama al-hayat al-dunya la'ib wa lahw*: That is, the worldly life is more like imaginary matters, of little benefit and quick to pass away.

*Wa zina*: That is, what a person adorns himself with of various kinds of adornment; adornment changes and passes away quickly.

*Wa tafakhur baynakum wa takathur fi al-amwal wal-awlad*: That is, it does not go beyond being play, diversion, adornment, boasting among you, and competition in wealth and children.

*Kamathal ghaythin a'jaba al-kuffara nabatuhu*: That is, its likeness in swift passing and in depriving its owner of the Hereafter and its bliss is like rain which pleased the kuffar, that is the farmers, by its plants, that is, by the crops that grew from it.

*Thumma yahiju fatarahu musfarran*: That is, it dries up, so you see it yellowed when its time of harvest has come.

*Thumma yakunu hutaman*: Then it quickly turns into dry debris that crumbles.

*Illa mata' al-ghurur*: That is, and the worldly life, in enjoying it, is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion, since life itself is delusion with no reality.

*Sabiqu ila maghfiratin min rabbikum*: That is, hasten to repentance, competing with others, so that your sins may be forgiven and you may enter the Garden of your Lord.

*Dhalika fadl Allah yu'tihi man yasha'*: That is, the promised forgiveness and Garden.

*Wallahu dhu al-fadl al-'azim*: That is, His bounty in what is promised is not far-fetched, though it is great.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues guiding and directing the believers to what increases their perfection and happiness in both lives. He addressed them saying: Know, O believers, whose hearts We have examined, that is, whose humility We have tested, since attachment to this world is the cause of heedlessness of the Hereafter and its requirements of remembrance and righteous deeds: ﴿Know that the life of this world is only play and amusement, adornment and boasting among yourselves, and competition in wealth and children﴾. This is its reality, and these are imaginary matters, of little benefit and quick to pass away. So do not be deceived by them, and do not let all of you turn entirely toward them; I advise you to that. For play and amusement produce no benefit that returns to the one who plays and amuses himself; adornment quickly changes, varies and vanishes; boasting among the boastful is mere talk with no lasting gain at all; and competition never ends at any limit, and it is gathered only through misery, toil and fatigue, and then it departs or is taken away, leaving no permanence or continuance, and it has consequences from which its owner cannot escape except by a mercy from God. And here is the likeness of the worldly life: it is ﴿like rain whose growth pleased the disbelievers﴾, that is, rain, ﴿whose growth pleased the disbelievers﴾, that is, the farmers who disbelieved, who sowed seed in the soil, ﴿its growth﴾ by which the rain grew, ﴿then it dries up and you see it turned yellow﴾ after days, ﴿then it becomes crumbled debris﴾ that crumbles. This is the world from its beginning to its painful end. As for the Hereafter, in it is severe punishment for the people of polytheism and sins, which they cannot avoid and from which they will be separated, and forgiveness and good pleasure from God for the people of monotheism and righteous deeds. The worldly life, although We have presented its likeness to you, is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion, that is, it has no reality, and all of its enjoyments that people take pleasure in are nothing but false delusion.

Therefore, I advise you: ﴿Hasten to forgiveness from your Lord﴾, that is, hasten to repentance, competing with one another so that your sins may be forgiven and you may enter the Garden of your Lord, ﴿whose breadth is like the breadth of the heaven and the earth, prepared for those who believe in God and His Messenger﴾, that is, made ready and presented, so it is prepared and readied. ﴿That is the bounty of God﴾, that is, the forgiveness and entry into the Garden, ﴿He gives it to whom He wills﴾. Whoever hastens to repentance, believes, does righteous deeds and abandons polytheism and sins, is among those whom His bounty wills, and therefore He grants him success in faith and righteous deeds. ﴿And God is the Possessor of great bounty﴾, so that which is sought and desired, salvation from the Fire and entry into the Garden, the abode of the righteous, should not be considered far-fetched from Him.

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of these verses:

1- A warning against being deceived by the worldly life.

2- A call to compete in seeking forgiveness of sin and entry into the Garden.

3- An explanation of the Garden and what earns it, which is faith in God and His messengers and its requirements of monotheism and righteous deeds.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 57, verses 22–25:

Explanation of the words:

﴿What befalls from a calamity on the earth﴾: that is, by drought and loss of wealth.

﴿Nor in yourselves﴾: that is, by illness and the loss of a child.

﴿Except that it is in a Book before We bring it into being﴾: that is, in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) before We create it.

﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾: that is, simple, not difficult.

﴿So that you do not despair over what has eluded you﴾: that is, so that you do not grieve over what has escaped you of the good you love.

﴿And do not exult in what He has given you﴾: that is, in what He has bestowed upon you, the exultation of arrogance (farah al-batar). As for the joy of gratitude (farah al-shukr), it is permitted.

﴿Allah does not love every arrogant boaster﴾: that is, one who is arrogant with his pride in what he has been given, boastful (fakhur) toward people.

﴿Those who are stingy﴾: that is, with what it was obligatory upon them to spend.

﴿And enjoin stinginess upon people﴾: that is, withholding what it was obligatory upon them to give.

﴿And whoever turns away﴾: that is, from faith, obedience, and accepting the admonitions of their Lord.

﴿Then indeed, Allah is the Free of need (al-Ghani)﴾: that is, free of need from all His creation, because His self-sufficiency is intrinsic to Him and He does not draw it from anything else.

﴿the Praiseworthy (al-Hamid)﴾: that is, praised for His majesty, His beauty, and His bounties and favours upon His servants.

﴿with clear proofs﴾: that is, with decisive arguments and demonstrations of the truth of their call.

﴿And We sent down with them the Book﴾: that is, We sent down to them the Scriptures containing the laws and rulings.

﴿and the Balance﴾: that is, justice, which the Scriptures were revealed to command and establish.

﴿that people may uphold justice﴾: that is, so that their lives among themselves may stand on the foundation of justice.

﴿In it is great might﴾: that is, in iron there is great might, and what is meant is instruments of warfare such as swords and other weapons.

﴿and benefits for people﴾: that is, people benefit from it, since there is no craft except that iron is its tool.

﴿And that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers unseen﴾: that is, and We sent down iron and placed in it great might so that Allah may know who supports His religion and His friends, and supports His messengers who convey His call from Him.

﴿unseen﴾: that is, while they do not see Him with their eyes in this world.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty﴾: that is, He has no need for anyone's support, and He only commanded it as an act of worship by which His servants draw near to Him.

Meanings of the verses:

The noble context continues in guiding and directing the believers toward what perfects and makes them happy. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿No disaster strikes upon the earth﴾, that is, no calamity befalls you, O believers, on the earth, by drought and famine, or flood, or blights that strike crops, ﴿nor within yourselves﴾, by illness and the loss of a child, ﴿except that it is in a Book﴾, that is, in the Book of Decrees, the Preserved Tablet, written with its quantity, its manner, its time, and its place, ﴿before We bring it into being﴾, that is, this is before Allah the Exalted creates and brings it into existence. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾, that is, His knowledge of it and His writing of it before its creation and its coming into being in its time is easy and simple for Allah.

And His saying: ﴿So that you do not despair﴾, that is, We have informed you of this after Our decree and judgment of it from eternity, so that you do not grieve over what has eluded you of the good you love in your worldly life, ﴿and do not exult in what He has given you﴾, the exultation of insolence and arrogance, for it is harmful. As for the joy of gratitude, there is no harm in it, for Allah may bless a servant so that he may be thankful.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah does not love every arrogant boaster﴾ warns His friends against two blameworthy traits that are not becoming to a believer: arrogance (al-ikhtiyal), that is, pride, and boasting over people with what Allah has given him and withheld from them. And His saying: ﴿Those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess upon people﴾ is an explanation of those whom Allah does not love: they are people of pride and boasting, described with two ugly qualities: stinginess, which is withholding what is obligatory, and enjoining stinginess and calling to it. They were not content with their own stinginess, so they commanded others to be stingy, that is, to withhold what is obligatory and not give it. We seek refuge with Allah from these four vices. And His saying: ﴿And whoever turns away﴾, that is, from faith and obedience, and from not accepting the admonition and guidance of Allah, ﴿then indeed Allah is the Free of need﴾ from all His creation, because His self-sufficiency is intrinsic to Him and He does not draw it from anything else, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, that is, praised for His majesty, His beauty, and His favour upon all His servants.

And the words of the Exalted: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs﴾, that is, with decisive arguments, and We sent down with them the Book containing the laws and rulings by which people are perfected and made happy, and We sent down the Balance, so that people may uphold justice, that is, so that their lives may stand on the foundation of justice and truth.

And the words of the Exalted: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾, that is, just as We sent down the Book for religion and the Balance for worldly life, We sent down iron for both together, for religion and for the world: in it is great might in wars, so it serves to establish religion through jihad, ﴿and benefits for people﴾, since all crafts depend upon it, so it serves the world.

And the words of the Exalted: ﴿And that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers unseen﴾, that is, among the wisdom in sending down iron is that Allah may know who supports Him, that is, supports His religion and His messengers through jihad with them and standing by their side, while they convey the call of their Lord ﴿unseen﴾, that is, while they do not see Allah the Exalted with their eyes, though they know Him in their hearts.

And the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty﴾ is an announcement that He has no need of the support of anyone among His creation, due to His intrinsic strength and His might that cannot be overcome. Rather, He has charged His servants with supporting His religion, His messengers, and His friends, as an honour and dignity for them, and so as to raise them by that to the station of martyrs.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the doctrine of divine decree and destiny (al-qada' wa'l-qadar).

2- Explanation of the wisdom in knowing divine decree and destiny and believing in them.

3- The prohibition of arrogance, boasting, stinginess, and enjoining stinginess.

4- Explanation of Allah's bounty and favour upon people through sending messengers, sending down Scriptures, the Balance, and iron, with its benefits for people and its great might.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 57, verse 29:

Explanation of the words:

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: i.e., in Jesus son of Mary and Moses before him.

﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَآمِنُوا بِرَسُولِهِ﴾: i.e., fear the punishment of God and believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) and follow him.

﴿يُؤْتِكُمْ كِفْلَيْنِ﴾: God will give you two portions of reward in return for your faith in your prophet and in Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ نُوراً تَمْشُونَ فِيهِ﴾: i.e., in this world, as you live under God's guidance, and in the Hereafter, when you walk by it upon the Sirat (al-Sirat, the bridge over Hellfire).

﴿لِّئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ﴾: i.e., so that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over any of God's bounty. The lam in "li-alla" is extra, added to strengthen the speech.

The meaning of the two verses:

This is God's address to the People of the Book, after He mentioned a summary of their messengers and their followers. He called those present among them by the title of faith, meaning: O you who have believed in the earlier messengers according to your claim, fear God and do not make distinctions between God's messengers, and believe in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). He will give you two portions (kiflayn), i.e., two shares and portions of His mercy and reward. He will also make for you a light by which you walk in this world, which is the Islamic guidance, for Islam is the straight path, whose follower neither goes astray nor is wretched; and by which you walk in the Hereafter over the Sirat to the Abode of Peace, Paradise. And He will forgive you your past and present sins, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. This is so that the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians who refused to believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) and to enter Islam, may know that they have no power over any of God's bounty, i.e., they cannot obtain any of God's bounty, and that bounty is in the hand of God, who gives it to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty.

Lessons from the two verses:

1. The greatest counsel offered to the People of the Book, if they would take it, is contained in God's address to them and in what He promised them in this noble verse.

2. The excellence of faith and piety, for they are the path to guardianship and honor in this world and the next.

3. The refutation of the claims of the People of the Book to monopolize Paradise, and informing them that they are barred from it unless they believe in the Messenger of God and fear God by performing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.
